subject: Telemetry consumption quota + exception gates for per-tenant cost/latency tiles

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Subject: Telemetry consumption quota + exception gates for per-tenant cost/latency tiles

Team —

Quick context: Acme AI asked for a per-tenant cost + tail-latency tile in Console that shows rolling burn (last 24h / 7d), the percent of requests served at full fidelity vs sampled, and SLA fallback events. Before we scope UX, we need a product+ops agreement on: sampling policy, hard telemetry quotas, and the exception/fallback gating matrix (what happens when a tenant hits budget or we detect runaway token churn).

Ask: can each of you reply with the constraints you need by EOD Friday so I can draft a short MR and attach to OBS-1427? Specifically: 
- Marissa: UX/product constraints — minimum data fidelity required for the tile to be useful, cardinality needs, and acceptable update cadence.
- Jordan: ops/telemetry cost impact — rough token/trace retention budget per tenant, cost delta for enabling full traces vs sampled traces, and preferred retention windows.
- Irene: instrumentation/runbook requirements — what we must ship in the SDK + server to support safe rollouts and automatic masking for PII.

I've attached a very rough gating worksheet (consumption-gates-draft.xlsx) with proposed thresholds and an initial canary rollout plan.

We should treat this as an exceptions-first design: when limits are breached, tile shows "degraded" state with exact fallback policy and a link to start a mitigation playbook (canary rollback, quota bump request, or synthetic fallback).

Thanks —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Telemetry consumption quota + exception gates for per-tenant cost/latency tiles

Thanks Naomi — good framing. A couple product constraints to call out up front: 

1) Minimum fidelity for the tile to be actionable: we need per-tenant 95th/99th latency percentiles and a rolling token burn (1h/24h/7d). Percentiles require histograms not raw traces; sampling is acceptable for 99th as long as we document sampling rate.

2) Cardinality: customers will want a tenant-level breakdown + ability to drill to a tenant->route path. We should cap drill depth in MVP to top 50 routes per tenant to keep storage bounded.

3) Update cadence: 1-minute ingest, 1-minute rollups for the 1h view, 15-minute rollups for 24h and 7d is fine for now. Anything slower hurts troubleshooting but faster pushes cost.

4) Degraded UX: If we enter a "degraded" telemetry mode (e.g., because of quota hit), show exact policy: a) switch percentiles to sampled estimates with clear banner b) show last known full-fidelity snapshot timestamp c) an action button to request a temporary quota bump (auto-triaged to CS/AcctOps).

I'll attach a quick CSV with a couple rough workload estimates so we can iterate on thresholds.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior PM, Observability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Telemetry consumption quota + exception gates for per-tenant cost/latency tiles

Sharing ops constraints / cost math from a telemetry perspective. TL;DR: full-fidelity traces (span-level + per-token logs) are ~8-12x the cost of compact histograms and sampled traces. Retention is the biggest driver.

Pointers: 
- Suggested default per-tenant telemetry budget (MVP): 100k tokens/day of full-fidelity equivalent, or 2M tokens/week for larger tenants. Above that, auto-switch to sampled traces at 10% rate.
- Retention windows: keep 24h full-fidelity hot window, 7d sampled, 30d aggregated histograms. Longer retention should be a paid add-on.
- Fallback mapping (proposal):
  * Normal: full-fidelity (hot retention 24h)
  * Exceeded soft threshold: 10% sampled traces + full histograms
  * Exceeded hard threshold (quota breached): 0% sampling for traces, histograms-only for percentiles; tile shows degraded banner and earliest snapshot timestamp

Cost estimate: enabling full fidelity for 1 large tenant for 7 days ~ additional $180/day infra cost (GPU+storage amortized). Small tenants are near negligible. If we have many large tenants we must throttle ingestion upstream.

Action items for me: add an alerting hook for when a tenant's 24h token consumption grows >3x week-over-week; create a playbook page (link below) that maps thresholds to ops runbooks.

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-consumption-gates (ops playbook draft)

-Jordan
Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: Telemetry consumption quota + exception gates for per-tenant cost/latency tiles

Couple instrumentation notes from my side: 

1) SDK flags: we need a tenant-level flag to toggle: full_traces | sampled_traces | histograms_only. This must be server-driven so we can flip during rollout without pushing client updates.
2) Masking: make masking a pre-ingest stage for any full-fidelity payloads (PII redaction rules + hashing for identifiers). We should ship a default mask list and allow tenant overrides (CVs, emails, unstructured blobs).
3) Canary rollout: suggest a three-step rollout for the new tile: internal alpha tenants (observability team), opt-in customers (select Acme), and then gradual ramp (10% of eligible tenants per day). The gate in the console should allow a manual "pause and rollback" by SRE/PM.

Runbook snippet to include in OBS-1427: 
- Detection: alert when token-burn > 2x expected baseline, or when histogram percentiles diverge >20% after switching to sampled traces.
- Immediate remediation: switch tenant to sampled_traces, send notification to tenant owner and CS, open an automated remediation run (ticket created + recommended actions).

I can prep the SDK flag PR and the masking tests. Schedule the 30-min sync and I will add a short instrumentation checklist to the Drive doc.

-Irene
